summary: Built and locally verified the disjoint-majority probe that the previous gap called for, and fixed the update so it carries a single interpretation (a stale 'explained' element had been re-applied each turn and kept superseding the violated account). The probe: A/B bootstrapped, A snapshots, adds a caught-up nonvoter E and voter C, then A is restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs so its configuration is the stale {A,B} while its log holds {A,B,C}; with B partitioned, AddVoter E succeeds (change_err nil) and the two-server change {A,B,E} commits on A plus E (entry index 11, A commit 11, same entry on E) — voter C silently dropped. B and C then elect B in term 4 while A is still leader in term 3, i.e. two concurrent leaders with disjoint support over the same log, and after the partition heals A's entry 11 becomes a LogNoop of term 4 instead of the committed configuration entry: a committed entry truncated on the node that committed it. Submitted with two comparisons (committed entry not truncated; at most one leader) against the new experiment; the construction-time run reproduced all of them, the harness is self-contained and was re-verified in an isolated copy of the captured tree, and the gap is answered with resolved=false pending the retained receipt.
